rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the most critical first step is to establish the simplest possible baseline to anchor all future comparisons. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the most minimal configuration in the space: a single RNA profile encoded with PCA (a fast, interpretable linear method). This tells us (1) whether RNA data alone carries sufficient signal for the task, (2) the performance floor against which more complex encoders (scvi, scgpt), multiprofile aggregation, and multimodal fusion must be judged, and (3) whether the task is solvable from a single modality at all. Establishing this floor first ensures that subsequent experiments—testing image-only, multimodal, or more sophisticated encoders—can be interpreted against a known reference rather than in a vacuum. Under a 10-experiment budget, spending one slot on the simplest baseline is the highest-information-per-experiment choice before exploring the richer design space.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → 48.5% acc), the dominant uncertainty is whether the image modality is informative at all and whether it could complement or outperform RNA. Config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) provides the cleanest direct comparison: same profile setting (single), a standard pretrained encoder (ResNet-50), isolating the modality effect. If image accuracy is comparable or better than RNA, multimodal fusion becomes a promising direction to exploit in later experiments. If image is substantially worse, we can focus remaining budget on improving RNA representations (scvi, scgpt) and aggregation. This single experiment reduces the most critical uncertainty with minimal confounding, making it the highest-information choice for experiment 2 of 10.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA n2000 single profile (config_001) achieved 0.485 accuracy, far outperforming image-only ResNet50 (config_010, 0.208), establishing RNA as the dominant modality. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether multiprofile aggregation can further improve the RNA signal, or whether the single-profile PCA representation is already near its ceiling. This experiment (config_002) tests the minimal extension of the best config by adding multiprofile + avgpool aggregation while keeping the same PCA n2000 encoder, isolating the effect of profile aggregation. It is the best use of experiment 3 because it directly exploits the strongest signal found so far, changes only one design axis (profile/aggregation), and will tell us whether to invest remaining budget in multiprofile variants (transformer aggregation, better encoders) or pivot toward encoder quality and multimodal fusion.

Evidence: RNA multiprofile with avgpool (config_002, acc=0.591) substantially outperforms RNA singleprofile (config_001, acc=0.485), while image-only (config_010, acc=0.208) is very weak. This confirms multiprofile RNA is the dominant signal. Uncertainty: We do not yet know whether transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool for multiprofile RNA. This experiment (config_003) directly compares transformer vs. avgpool aggregation while holding all other factors constant (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000), isolating the aggregation effect. This is the best next step because it is a clean, single-variable comparison in the most promising region, and the result will inform whether to invest remaining budget in transformer-based aggregation for downstream multimodal or encoder experiments.

Evidence: RNA dominates (0.485-0.591 vs 0.208 for image), and the best config so far is rna_only/multiprofile/pca_n2000/avgpool at 0.591. Multiprofile+avgpool clearly outperforms singleprofile and transformer aggregation. Question: Can a more expressive RNA encoder (scgpt, a pretrained single-cell foundation model) improve on PCA's linear projection while keeping the proven multiprofile+avgpool pipeline? This isolates the encoder effect with all other settings held at their best-known values. Why this is the best use of experiment 5: It directly tests whether the current 0.591 ceiling is due to PCA's limitations or is a fundamental limit of the RNA-only pipeline, which determines whether to invest remaining budget in better encoders or pivot to multimodal fusion. With 5 experiments left, establishing the RNA encoder ceiling before adding fusion complexity is the most informative next step.

The best result so far is config_002 (RNA-only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) at 0.591 accuracy. Image alone is very weak (0.208), but it may carry complementary information not captured by RNA. The critical open question is whether multimodal fusion can surpass the best RNA-only baseline. Config_018 directly extends config_002 by adding the resnet50 image branch with the same multiprofile/avgpool settings and simple concat fusion, isolating the effect of fusion without changing any other design choice. If it beats 0.591, the remaining 4 experiments can exploit the multimodal direction (e.g., try weighted fusion, ViT encoder, or better RNA encoders). If it does not, we can confidently focus remaining budget on RNA-only refinements (e.g., scvi_n200 with multiprofile/avgpool). This is the highest-information experiment because it determines which branch of the search space to commit the remaining budget to.

The current best is config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) at 0.619 acc. The image-only baseline is very weak (0.208), suggesting the image modality contributes limited signal and may be better served by a learned weighting rather than a fixed concatenation. config_019 is a clean single-variable comparison to config_018, isolating fusion strategy (weighted vs concat) while holding all other settings constant. This directly tests whether the model can learn to down-weight the weaker image branch and up-weight the stronger RNA branch, which is the most impactful architectural question given the large modality imbalance. With 3 experiments remaining, resolving the fusion question now allows the next two to either exploit the better fusion with a stronger image encoder (ViT) or confirm the current best, making this the highest-information-use experiment under the budget.

The current best is config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted; acc=0.639). The image modality alone is weak (ResNet50: 0.208), yet it still adds ~5% over RNA-only in the multimodal setting, suggesting the image features contribute useful complementary signal. The most natural single-variable extension is to upgrade the image encoder from ResNet50 to ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L while keeping everything else identical (pca_n2000, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion). This isolates the effect of image representation quality. If ViT-L provides richer spatial/texture features, it should push accuracy above 0.639; if not, it confirms the bottleneck is elsewhere. With only 2 experiments remaining, this is the highest-value exploitation of the current best direction, and it avoids the transformer aggregation which was clearly inferior to avgpool in all RNA-only comparisons (0.519 vs 0.591).

The current best is config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) at 0.6390 accuracy. The strongest evidence shows weighted fusion > concat, avgpool > transformer, multiprofile > singleprofile, and pca_n2000 > scgpt in RNA-only. However, scvi_n200 has never been tested in any experiment. Config_031 is a single-variable change from the current best (swapping pca_n2000 → scvi_n200 while keeping all other proven-optimal settings: resnet50, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile). This isolates the effect of the RNA encoder in the multimodal context and tests whether a learned variational representation can capture complementary biological signal that PCA misses. It is the best use of this experiment because it directly challenges the current best with a minimal, well-motivated perturbation; if it succeeds it pushes past 0.6390, and if it fails we retain config_019 as the top result with one experiment remaining for a final refinement.

The current best is config_031 (scvi_n200, resnet50, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted) at 0.6776. The evidence shows scvi_n200 is a strong RNA encoder (0.678 vs 0.639 for pca_n2000 in the same multimodal setting), avgpool outperforms transformer, and weighted fusion beats concat. The one untested dimension on top of config_031 is the image encoder: in the pca_n2000 setting, resnet50 (0.639) and imagenet_vit_l (0.635) were close, but with the stronger scvi_n200 RNA representation the interaction with a higher-capacity image encoder (ViT-L) may shift. config_037 changes only the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l, isolating that effect. As the final experiment, this is the highest-probability single-variable extension to potentially exceed 0.678, while avoiding the clearly inferior transformer aggregation or the weaker scgpt encoder.
